title: RWB-DM-013 names three entities and a cutover step but no owner, source, format or sign-off place after the realignment
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3.md (RWB-DM-013); _work/msr/context/P1.md ownership rows; FSD P1 v3 A2.2 and A2.11; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 and T3.6
section: Story, Preconditions, Business rules, Data, Contract 12.7, Test cases
description: The legacy story migrates recovery_case, proceeds and write_off with one cutover step, and its Endpoints section says the migration is run by the recovery service identity. After the realignment rwb-source-data owns none of the three tables (the P1 ownership rows list 18 tables, without proceeds, write_off or recovery_case), so the story can only extract and hand over; no source document states which service holds proceeds, write_off or the closure facts, where the legacy dump is read from, in what format the parts are handed over, where the data steward signs off, or what the ten clean days are counted on. The combined row covers every such value in this story.
evidence: Context pack P1 ownership rows: 18 tables, none of them proceeds, write_off or recovery_case. Legacy RWB-DM-013 Endpoints: 'No endpoint in this story. The migration is a cutover step run by the recovery service identity'. FSD P1 v3 A2.2 DP13: 'Money and closure | ACE (ingested from ALS and GL) | v_ace_payment, v_ace_write_off | proceeds, write_off'. FSD P1 v3 A2.11 REC-05: every account_key, person_key, asset_key and payment_code resolved 'on a Workbench table'.
proposed: Accept the split: P1 extracts once and hands over, rwb-payment loads proceeds into rwb_payment, rwb-writeoff loads write_off into rwb_writeoff, rwb-case loads the closure facts with the case row, the dump is the legacy cutover dump read once, the handover is a file with a checksum, the sign-off sits in the cutover record of the release pipeline, and the ten clean days are PASS reconciliation results on reconciliation_result. Confirm the owners and the handover format at the wave-4 build review.
